later: You can repeat any of these steps from Settings.

gitd.name: gitd
gitd.title: gitd
gitd.description: gitd creates each agent's workspace and publishes with the token it holds, so agents never get it.
gitd.hint: gitd is not running. Start it and check again.
gitd.accessDenied: Your user does not have permission to talk to gitd yet. Sign out of Windows and back in (or restart), then press “Check again”.
gitd.notRunning: gitd cannot be found: it is not installed or not running. Install and start it, then press “Check again”.

isolation.name: Isolation
isolation.title: Agent isolation
isolation.description: Agents run confined so they cannot read your keys or your git configuration. Without isolation brnch does not start them.
isolation.unknown: The isolation state could not be read.
isolation.passwordValue: Random, kept by brnch for you
isolation.adminWarning: Windows will ask for administrator permission once. If you refuse, brnch will not run agents: it does not start them without isolation.

agents.name: Agents
agents.title: Installed agents
agents.description: brnch looks for the agents on this machine.
agents.missing: Claude Code was not found. Install it and check again.

project.name: Project
project.title: Your first project
project.description: A project is a repository. Add one to start working with agents.

credential.name: Publishing
credential.title: Connect your GitHub account
credential.description: To publish, gitd needs access to your repositories. Choose how to connect it; you can change it or add another account later in Settings.
credential.reachable: gitd answers. Connect an account so it can publish.
credential.needsGitd: gitd must be running to hold the credential.
credential.note: The agent only asks to publish; gitd pushes with this token and applies its policy.
